topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology lecture series, student cohorts, and the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer as a Disruption of Developmental Differentiation and Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cumulative genetic and epigenetic changes cause cells to fail their developmental programs and disrupt normal tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the histological and clinical criteria that distinguish benign from malignant tumors through the processes of tissue invasion, metastasis, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the standard naming rules and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue origins.

topics.label: Clinical Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the mechanical, metabolic, and organ-destructive mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Tumor Incidence in Humans and Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological prevalence and mortality of tumors in human populations alongside the evolutionary occurrence of neoplasia across animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, histological requirements, and relative efficacy of screening programs designed to detect pre-malignant and early malignant lesions.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and framing upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
